D018-D020_h025.question:
It started after the car accident last spring—so it’s been about eight months now, and it hasn’t really eased up. I was driving home from school when a truck ran the red light and hit my side. I wasn’t badly hurt, but ever since then, anything that reminds me of it sets me off. If I hear screeching brakes or see a truck suddenly pull out, my chest tightens, my heart races, and it feels like I’m right back there, about to be hit again. Even just thinking about driving alone can make me panic.

What’s been hardest is how angry I’ve become. It’s like there’s this constant irritation simmering under the surface. I snap at my students for small things, like tapping a pencil, and then feel awful afterward. At home, I’ll explode at my husband over something tiny—dishes in the sink, a comment taken the wrong way—and I don’t fully understand why I go from zero to a hundred so fast.

And when something does go well—like a lesson the kids love or good feedback from my principal—I don’t really feel proud or happy. It’s like I’m numb to any sense of satisfaction, just waiting for the next thing to set me off.
